children: Otsuka Holdings' revenue growth from wholly owned products is likely to help boost profitability, Jefferies analysts say in a note. Consensus appears to be underestimating the margin impact of an improving product mix, the U.S. bank says. Voyxact, a kidney disease drug, and other wholly-owned assets are replacing partnered products as the Japanese pharmaceutical company's main revenue drivers, Jefferies says. As this transition continues, the bank expects profit to grow faster than revenue. Jefferies raises its target price on Otsuka to 14,000 yen from Y12,700. Shares are 0.3% higher at Y11,770. (kosaku.narioka@wsj.com; @kosakunarioka)
